subject.name: Robot Money Allocation
subject.thesis_blurb: The Robot Money vault's published allocation framework: four buckets (Conservative DeFi Yield 95% / Agent Tokens 5% / Protocol Tokens 0% / Real World Assets 0%) and the constituents inside each bucket. The committee reviews the targets themselves — are the bucket weights right for the regime, and within each bucket are the right constituents weighted correctly? This subject is the framework, not the holdings. The vault subject reviews holdings; this one reviews targets.
structural_notes: no portfolio to scrape — the subject IS the allocation.json framework state
the committee should never default to 'targets are right because they are targets' — reflect on the regime, the research, market conditions, and any item-level read you can support
recommendations cover BOTH the between-bucket mix (95/5/0/0) AND the within-bucket constituents (e.g., inside Conservative DeFi, how should Aave/Compound/Morpho/Sky split?)
the vault subject (robotmoney-vault) reviews how the actual holdings drift from these targets; this subject reviews whether the targets themselves should change

research._comment: Curated summaries of Robot Money published research. The brief generator injects this into Athena's prompt only — research is Athena's context. Each article carries a `core` flag: core articles (methodology, frameworks, risk taxonomies, definitions) stay in Athena's context permanently. Non-core articles (quarterly reads, post-mortems on specific events) slide on a most-recent-N window. Athena's context = all core + most-recent non-core, capped at 15 total. Add `core: true` for foundational pieces; omit for time-bound ones.

articles.title: Treasury Allocation for On-Chain Businesses
articles.summary: 8-year backtest comparing regime-based 3-state allocation against HODL strategies (ETH, SP500) and stable yield, across a full market cycle.
key_findings: Regime-based allocation outperformed straight HODL on a risk-adjusted basis (higher Sharpe, lower max drawdown) across the 2018-2026 window.
Most of the alpha came from being de-risked in the 2022 drawdown phase, not from being aggressively risk-on in mania phases.
The 3-state model (risk-off / neutral / risk-on) captured most of the cycle alpha; finer-grained regimes added complexity without proportional improvement.

articles.title: Backtesting honestly: what survives when you remove hindsight
articles.summary: Discovered the regime model's inverse-correlation weighting was computed with full-history hindsight. Rebuilt it point-in-time and re-ran every comparison.
key_findings: Hindsight-weighted backtests overstated alpha by a material margin; the honest version is what the live model now uses.
The macro panel correlation signal held up under point-in-time weights; the on-chain panel signal was weaker but still directional.
Honest 8-year CAGR of the regime-based allocation is meaningfully positive but not the eye-popping figure the hindsight version produced.

articles.title: Conservative vs aggressive: combining macro and on-chain regime signals
articles.summary: Backtested two ways to combine macro + on-chain panels into a single composite — conservative (any panel off → off) vs aggressive (any panel on → on, unless contradicted).
key_findings: Conservative composite captures most of the drawdown protection with lower turnover.
Aggressive composite captures more upside in 2021-style melt-ups but produces more whipsaw losses in choppy regimes.
The current live model uses the conservative composite — costs some upside but keeps drawdowns shallower.

articles.title: Regime Detection
articles.summary: Prior art, methods, and data sources for risk-on / risk-off regime classification used by the Robot Money regime model.
key_findings: Composite is built from 18 indicators across macro (10) and on-chain (8) panels.
Each indicator is percentile-ranked over a rolling 3-year window, sign-aligned so high = risk-on, weighted by inverse correlation within panel.
Bucket thresholds: composite percentile <0.33 = risk-off, 0.33-0.67 = neutral, >0.67 = risk-on.

articles.title: Smart Contract Risks
articles.summary: Field guide to how DeFi vaults get exploited. Chronological case studies relevant to the Conservative DeFi Yield bucket's protocol selection.
key_findings: Vault exploits cluster around three patterns: oracle manipulation, reentrancy via callback hooks, and admin-key compromise.
Aave, Compound, and Morpho (current Conservative DeFi protocols) have multi-year track records without principal loss events.
Concentration in a single protocol within the Conservative bucket is the bigger risk than the bucket itself.

recent_sessions.synthesis: The three voices converge on the regime mechanics — composite 0.578 at the 70th percentile, eighth session in risk_on but drifting toward neutral, with the panel split (macro 82nd, factor 96th, on-chain 15th) doing the load-bearing work and on-chain having deteriorated 16 points in three sessions while the correlation card flags it as the forward-loaded crypto panel. They diverge on what that widening dissent implies for 95/5/0/0. Athena reads the on-chain sub-20th as the historical setup that resolves down and would cut Agent Tokens to 3% while fast-tracking a 5% RWA sleeve to fill the counter-cycle gap; Robot Money holds 95/5/0/0 as mandate-correct and warns that tilting inside the 0.33-0.67 band is the exact whipsaw the conservative composite was built to avoid; Woon funds Agent Tokens to the full 5% and argues that trimming on the on-chain print double-counts a signal the composite has already absorbed. Within Conservative DeFi the rough alignment is Aave and Morpho leading at ~30-35% each with Sky mid and Compound capped, though Morpho-versus-Aave ordering remains unsettled. The contested call is again the Agent Tokens weight — 3 versus 5 versus full 5 — and what settles it is whether the on-chain panel clears the 33rd for five consecutive sessions (resolves toward Woon) or stays sub-20th while composite drifts back toward neutral (resolves toward Athena, with Robot Money holding target throughout).

The three voices converged on the regime mechanics — composite 0.608 at the 84th percentile, risk_on by label but softening from 0.631 over eight sessions, with the panel split (macro 88th, factor 98th, on-chain 31st) doing the load-bearing work — and diverged on what the on-chain dissent implies, since on-chain is the panel the correlation card flags as forward-loaded on crypto. On the framework, Athena reads the on-chain sub-33rd as a reason to trim Agent Tokens to 3% and fast-track RWA; Robot Money holds 95/5/0/0 as mandate-correct and warns that tilting on top of an already-conservative composite double-counts the signal; Woon reads the same percentile as a green light to fund Agent Tokens to 6-7% from Conservative before the window closes. Within Conservative DeFi there is rough alignment on Aave and Morpho leading with Sky and Compound capped, though the exact split is unsettled. The contested call is the Agent Tokens weight — 3 versus 5 versus 7 — and what settles it is whether the on-chain panel clears the 33rd threshold for multiple sessions (resolves toward Woon) or stays sub-threshold while composite drifts toward 0.67 (resolves toward Athena, with Robot Money holding target throughout).

The committee converges on the regime mechanics — composite 0.617 at the 86th percentile is risk_on by label, but all three voices flag the same structural tell: macro 92nd and factor 99th versus on-chain 26th, a panel split that makes the load-bearing crypto signal the dissenter on an otherwise mania-coded tape. They diverge on what that asymmetry implies for the 95/5/0/0 frame. Athena would trim Agent Tokens to ~3% pending on-chain confirmation and flags RWA at 0% as the bigger structural gap; Robot Money holds 95/5/0/0 as mandate-correct given no governance signal to deviate; Woon reads the same percentile as underweight and pushes Agent Tokens to 7-8% funded from Conservative. Within Conservative DeFi there is rough alignment on tilting Aave and Morpho heavier and capping Sky and Compound, though Athena and Woon disagree on whether Aave or Morpho leads. The contested call is the Agent Tokens weight itself — what settles it is the on-chain panel clearing the 33rd threshold (resolves toward Woon) or failing to (resolves toward Athena).
